  <div style="text-align: left; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">To the shareholders and the Board of Directors of Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc.</div>

  <div style="text-align: left; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Opinion on the Financial Statements</div>

  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. and subsidiaries (the "Company") as of July 28,
    2023, and July 29, 2022, and the related consolidated statements of income, consolidated statements of comprehensive income, consolidated statements of changes in shareholders' equity, and consolidated statements of cash flows, for each of the three
    years in the period ended July 28, 2023, and the related notes&#160;(collectively referred to as the "financial statements"). In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of July
    28, 2023, and July 29, 2022, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended July 28, 2023, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</div>

  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We have also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB), the Company's
    internal control over financial reporting as of July 28, 2023, based on criteria established in <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Internal Control &#8212; Integrated Framework (2013)</span> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring
    Organizations of the Treadway Commission and our report dated September 26, 2023, expressed an unqualified opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting.</div>

  <div style="text-align: left; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Change in Accounting Principle</div>

  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As discussed in Note 1 to the financial statements, the Company has changed its method of accounting for debt with conversion options as of July 31,
    2021, due to adoption of Accounting Standards Update No. 2020-06, <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Debt - Debt with Conversion and Other Options (Subtopic 470-20) and Derivatives and Hedging - Contracts in Entity's Own Equity
      (Subtopic 815-40): Accounting for Convertible Instruments and Contracts in an Entity's Own Equity</span><span style="font-size: 10pt;">.</span></div>

  <div style="text-align: left; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Basis for Opinion</div>

  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company's management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's financial
    statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the
    Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</div>

  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable
    assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error
    or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting
    principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</div>

  <div style="text-align: left; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Critical Audit Matter</div>

  <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The critical audit matter communicated below is a matter arising from the current-period audit of the financial statements that was communicated or required to be
    communicated to the audit committee and that (1) relates to accounts or disclosures that are material to the financial statements and (2) involved our especially challenging, subjective, or complex judgments. The communication of critical audit matters
    does not alter in any way our opinion on the financial statements, taken as a whole, and we are not, by communicating the critical audit matter below, providing a separate opinion on the critical audit matter or on the accounts or disclosures to which
    it relates.</div>

  <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"> <br />
  </div>

  <div class="BRPFPageBreakArea" style="clear: both; margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 10pt;">
    <div class="BRPFPageNumberArea" style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal;">47</span></div>

    <div class="BRPFPageBreak" style="page-break-after: always;">
      <hr style="border-width: 0px; clear: both; margin: 4px 0px; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000;" /></div>

    <div class="BRPFPageHeader" style="width: 100%;">
      <div><a href="#PAGE"><span style="font-size: 8pt; font-style: italic;">Table of Contents</span></a></div>

    </div>

  <div style="text-align: left; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Commitments and Contingencies &#8211;
      Insurance Reserves &#8211; Refer to Notes 1 and 14 to the financial </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';">statements</span></div>

  <div style="text-align: left; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Critical Audit Matter Description</div>

  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company self-insures a significant portion of its workers&#8217; compensation and general liability program and records a reserve for all unresolved
    claims and an estimate of incurred but not reported (IBNR) claims. These reserves and estimates of IBNR claims are based upon a full-scope actuarial study performed annually by management&#8217;s specialist at the end of the third quarter and are adjusted by
    the actuarially determined losses and actual claims payments for the fourth quarter. The reserves and losses in the actuarial study represent a range of possible outcomes within which no given estimate is more likely than any other estimate. Using this
    information, the Company records the expected losses in the lower half of the range, which is discounted to present value using a risk-free interest rate. The Company also monitors actual claims development as another means of estimating the adequacy
    of the historical reserves.</div>

  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We identified insurance reserves as a critical audit matter because estimating the reserve for all unresolved claims and IBNR claims involves
    significant estimation by management. This required a high degree of auditor judgment and an increased extent of effort, including the need to involve our actuarial specialists, when performing audit procedures to evaluate whether insurance reserves
    were appropriately recorded as of July 28, 2023<span style="font-size: 10pt;">.</span></div>

  <div style="text-align: left; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">How the Critical Audit Matter Was Addressed in the Audit</div>

  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our audit procedures related to the insurance reserves included the following, among others:</div>

  <div>
    <table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; text-align: left; color: #000000;" class="DSPFListTable">

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Basis of Presentation</span></div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c36860606" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c36860607"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FiscalPeriod" id="Text_7d847485b2e444be9e662cad92f623b2" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; color: #000000;">Fiscal year &#8211; </span>The Company&#8217;s fiscal
      year ends on the Friday nearest July 31st and each quarter consists of thirteen weeks unless noted otherwise.&#160; References in these Notes to a year or quarter are to the Company&#8217;s fiscal year or quarter unless noted otherwise.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c36860607" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c36860608">

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">GAAP &#8211; The accompanying Consolidated Financial Statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted
        accounting principles in the U.S. (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;).</div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c36860609" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606010">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606010" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606011"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_a430cf664b7e4010afd5db1c697cbed3" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Principles of consolidation &#8211; The Consolidated Financial Statements include the accounts of the Company and its
      subsidiaries, all of which are wholly owned.&#160; All significant intercompany transactions and balances have been eliminated.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606011" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606012">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;&#160;</div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606012" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606013"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="Text_256bcb1b84914833bd960a6248c6eb03" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Use of estimates &#8211; Management of the Company has made certain estimates and assumptions relating to the reporting of
      assets and liabilities and the disclosure of contingent liabilities at the date of the Consolidated Financial Statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting periods to prepare these Consolidated Financial Statements
      in conformity with GAAP.&#160; Management believes that such estimates have been based on reasonable and supportable assumptions and that the resulting estimates are reasonable for use in the preparation of the Consolidated Financial Statements.&#160; Actual
      results, however, could differ from those estimates.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

    <div style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606013" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606014">
<div>&#160;
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
<div style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">
        <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606014" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606015"><ix:nonNumeric name="cbrl:ExternalImpactsToOperatingEnvironmentPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_1d01cc706cc7405e85971091d9d491cf" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">External impacts to the Company&#8217;s operating environment &#8211; The Company&#8217;s operating results have been impacted by the
          COVID-19 pandemic and other macroeconomic conditions.&#160; During 2021, the Company&#8217;s business began recovering from the COVID-19 pandemic, but the Company continued to see negative impacts on the Company&#8217;s sales and traffic as a result of both
          changes in consumer behavior and federal, state and local governmental authorities&#8217; continuation of various restrictions on travel, group gatherings and dine-in services.&#160; Dining room service was operational to varying degrees, yet most locations
          were impacted at times by capacity restrictions, social distancing guidelines, and decreased consumer demand for in-person dining.&#160; In 2022, the Company continued to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic; however, the Company believes outbreaks of
          new variants adversely impacted consumer demand in 2022.&#160; While the Company&#8217;s dining rooms operated without COVID-related restrictions in 2023, it is possible that renewed outbreaks, increases in cases and/or new variants of the disease, either
          as part of a national trend or on a more localized basis, could result in COVID-19-related restrictions including capacity restrictions or otherwise limit the Company&#8217;s dine-in services, or negatively affect consumer demand.&#160; In 2023 and 2022,
          the Company experienced inflationary conditions with respect to the cost for food, ingredients, retail merchandise, transportation, distribution, labor and utilities resulting, in part, from economic pressures related to the COVID-19 pandemic.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
        </div>

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606017" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606018">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <br />
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606018" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606019"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_aa5542dcf705458cbca963f6fcc0f625" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Cash and cash equivalents &#8211; The Company&#8217;s policy is to consider all highly liquid investments purchased with an original
      maturity of three months or less to be cash equivalents.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606019" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606020">
<div style="text-align: left; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606020" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606021"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:TradeAndOtherAccountsReceivablePolicy" id="Text_19036fd22ca94e0686f09dfc37b942e5" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Accounts receivable &#8211; Accounts receivable represent their estimated net realizable value.&#160; Accounts receivable are
      written off when they are deemed uncollectible.&#160;</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606021" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606022">

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606022" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606023"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:InventoryPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_66219ee62cb24358ac1c4c5521246f73" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_af2c728a99e6419f84a9f92342dcdcd51">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Inventories &#8211; Cost of restaurant inventory is determined by the first-in, first-out (&#8220;FIFO&#8221;) method.&#160; Retail inventories
      are valued using the retail inventory method (&#8220;RIM&#8221;) except at the retail distribution center which are valued using moving average cost.&#160; Approximately <ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:PercentageOfRetailInventoriesValuedUsingRetailInventoryMethod" id="Fact_5f3be529bd1a47ccadc900258482fe95" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U004" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">60</ix:nonFraction>%
      of retail inventories are valued using RIM.&#160; Retail inventories valued using RIM are stated at the lower of cost or market.&#160; Cost of restaurant inventory and retail inventory valued using moving average cost are stated at the lower of cost and net
      realizable value.&#160; See Note 3 for additional information regarding the components of inventory.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606023" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606024"><ix:continuation id="Text_af2c728a99e6419f84a9f92342dcdcd51" continuedAt="Text_af2c728a99e6419f84a9f92342dcdcd52">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606024" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606025"><ix:continuation id="Text_af2c728a99e6419f84a9f92342dcdcd52">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Valuation provisions are included for retail inventory obsolescence, retail inventory shrinkage, returns and
      amortization of certain items.&#160; The estimate of retail inventory shrinkage is adjusted upon physical inventory counts.&#160; Annual physical inventory counts are conducted based upon a cyclical inventory schedule.&#160; An estimate of shrinkage is recorded for
      the time period between physical inventory counts by using a <ix:nonNumeric name="cbrl:PeriodOfAveragePhysicalInventoryUsedForEstimateOfShrinkage" id="Fact_4a06c9069a9648bd9152e2c84b1954ed" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">two-year</ix:nonNumeric> average of the physical inventories&#8217; results on a store-by-store
      basis.</div>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_4b9c2a16129749f4800dd09d63603752" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true"><ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606041" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606042">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Impairment of long-lived assets &#8211; T</span>he Company assesses the impairment of long-lived assets whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying value of an asset may not be
      recoverable.&#160; Recoverability of assets is measured by comparing the carrying value of the asset to the undiscounted future cash flows expected to be generated by the asset.&#160; If the total expected future cash flows are less than the carrying value of
      the asset, the carrying value is written down, for an asset to be held and used, to the estimated fair value or, for an asset to be disposed of, to the fair value, net of estimated costs of disposal.&#160; Any loss resulting from impairment is recognized
      by a charge to income.&#160; During 2023, <ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:NumberOfLocationsDeterminedToBeImpaired" id="Fact_86da4787e9824054a32139a543a849cb" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U005" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">six</ix:nonFraction> Cracker Barrel locations were determined to be impaired and the Company recorded an impairment
      charge of $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseImpairmentLoss" id="Fact_bd29c1ea2ad245eda05de0a22ec40955" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">11,692</ix:nonFraction>, which is included in the impairment and store closing costs line on the Consolidated Statement of Income<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">.</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606043" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606044"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_1aaf3692dc4b4e30a7c392d36de5e24a" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_ed31873ea145429989ced4f1e0ea8de81">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Goodwill and other intangible assets &#8211; The Company accounts for all transactions that represent business combinations using the
      acquisition method of accounting, where the identifiable assets acquired and the liabilities assumed are recognized and measured at their fair values on the date the Company obtains control in the acquiree.&#160; Such fair values that are not finalized
      for reporting periods following the acquisition date are estimated and recorded as estimated amounts.&#160; Adjustments to these estimated amounts during the measurement period (defined as the date through which all information required to identify and
      measure the consideration transferred, the assets acquired and the liabilities assumed has been obtained, limited to one year from the acquisition date) are recorded when identified.&#160; Goodwill is determined as the excess of the fair value of the
      consideration conveyed in the acquisition over the fair value of the net assets acquired.&#160; Goodwill and other intangibles are evaluated for impairment annually on June 1 or more frequently if events occur or circumstances change that, more likely
      than not, reduce the fair value of the reporting unit below its carrying value.&#160; At July 28, 2023 and July 29, 2022, the Company does not have any reporting units that are at risk of failing step one of the impairment test.&#160; At both July 28, 2023 and
      July 29, 2022, goodwill of $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:Goodwill" id="Fact_318ce9152b7d4c24890b604fc41ecabb" contextRef="c20220729_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_MapleStreetBiscuitCompanyMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:Goodwill" id="Fact_452953b093fb4e56a0bfd6aa7564d81b" contextRef="c20230728_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_MapleStreetBiscuitCompanyMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">4,690</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> consisted of the Company&#8217;s acquisition of its <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionPercentageOfVotingInterestsAcquired" id="Fact_2ad80aaef7c54bf3abf6e0fccbf90347" contextRef="c20220729_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_MapleStreetBiscuitCompanyMember" unitRef="U004" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionPercentageOfVotingInterestsAcquired" id="Fact_19867e21993440049b99d4845ded5e8e" contextRef="c20230728_BusinessAcquisitionAxis_MapleStreetBiscuitCompanyMember" unitRef="U004" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">100</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>% ownership of Maple Street Biscuit Company (&#8220;MSBC&#8221;), a breakfast and lunch fast casual concept. </div>

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Convertible Senior Notes &#8211; In June 2021, the Company completed a $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" id="Fact_d54e8359d41c424baed0415df4d9b95d" contextRef="c20210618_DebtInstrumentAxis_Zero625PercentConvertibleSeniorNotesDue2026Member" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">300,000</ix:nonFraction> principal aggregate amount private offering of <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" id="Fact_ecc8cf2a569a4b0b801b3fdd9a91f7bb" contextRef="c20210618_DebtInstrumentAxis_Zero625PercentConvertibleSeniorNotesDue2026Member" unitRef="U004" decimals="5" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.625</ix:nonFraction>% convertible Senior
      Notes due in 2026 (the &#8220;Notes&#8221;). In accordance with accounting guidance on embedded conversion features indexed to and settled in equity, the Company valued and bifurcated the conversion option associated with the Notes from the respective host debt
      instrument. The carrying amount of the equity is recorded as a debt discount and represents the difference between the proceeds from the issuance of the Notes and the fair value of the liability component of the Notes. The significant assumptions
      used in the fair value of the liability component of the Notes were risk-free rate, discount rate based on the Company&#8217;s implied credit spread and term of the Notes, expected volatility of the Company&#8217;s stock price and dividend yield. The resulting
      debt discount on the Notes is amortized to interest expense using the effective interest method over the contractual term of the Notes. In addition, the debt issuance costs related to the issuance of the Notes were allocated between the liability and
      equity components based on their relative values. Debt issuance costs attributable to the liability component were recorded as a contra-liability and are presented net against the Notes balance on the Company&#8217;s consolidated balance sheets. These
      costs are amortized to interest expense using the effective interest method over the term of the Notes.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 24px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">Due to the Company&#8217;s adoption of new accounting guidance for convertible instruments on July 31, 2021, the Company no longer bifurcates the Notes into a liability and an equity component in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets.
        Upon adoption of this new accounting guidance, the Notes are accounted for entirely as a liability, and the issuance costs of the Notes are accounted for wholly as debt issuance costs. The equity conversion feature that was recorded to equity, as
        well as the unamortized debt discount and amortization expense attributable to equity, have been derecognized.</span></div>

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">D</span><span style="display: inline; float: none; letter-spacing: normal; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 24px; text-transform: none;"><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">e</span>rivative instruments and hedging activities &#8211; The Company is exposed to market risk, such as changes in interest rates and commodity prices.&#160; The Company has interest rate
        risk relative to its outstanding borrowings under the revolving credit facility (see Note 4).&#160; The Company&#8217;s policy has been to manage interest cost using a mix of fixed and variable rate debt.&#160; To manage this risk in a cost-efficient manner, prior
        to 2022, the Company used derivative instruments, specifically interest rate swaps.&#160; In the fourth quarter of 2021, the Company terminated all of its interest rate swaps and issued the Notes (see discussion above under &#8220;Convertible Senior Notes&#8221;
        and Note 5 for further information).</span></div>

<div style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; text-transform: none;"><span style="font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 24px; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">Prior to the termination of the interest rate swaps in the fourth quarter of 2021, all of the Company&#8217;s interest rate swaps were accounted for as cash flow hedges.&#160; For derivative instruments that were designated
        and qualify as a cash flow hedge, the gain or loss on the derivative instrument was reported as a component of other comprehensive income and reclassified into earnings in the same period during which the hedged transaction affected earnings and
        was presented in the same statement of income line item as the earnings effect of the hedged item. Gains and losses on the derivative instrument representing hedge components excluded from the assessment of effectiveness, if any, are recognized
        currently in earnings in the same statement of income line item as the earnings effect of the hedged item.&#160; The Company did not elect to reclassify income tax effects resulting from the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act to retained earnings; income tax effects
        are released on an individual basis to income tax expense.</span></div>

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Companies may elect whether or not to offset related assets and liabilities and report the net amount on their financial
      statements if the right of setoff exists.&#160; Under a master netting agreement, the Company has the legal right to offset the amounts owed to the Company against amounts owed by the Company under a derivative instrument that exists between the Company
      and a counterparty.&#160; When the Company is engaged in more than one outstanding derivative transaction with the same counterparty and also has a legally enforceable master netting agreement with that counterparty, its credit risk exposure is based on
      the net exposure under the master netting agreement.&#160; If, on a net basis, the Company owes the counterparty, the Company regards its credit exposure to the counterparty as being <ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:CreditExposureToCounterpartyIfCompanyOwesCounterparty" id="Fact_73fc0c39a4354f339361ff2d5f77bc99" contextRef="c20230728" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">zero</ix:nonFraction>.</div>

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Unredeemed gift cards and certificates &#8211; Unredeemed gift cards and certificates represent a liability of the Company

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Revenue recognition &#8211; Revenue consists primarily of sales from restaurant and retail operations.&#160; The Company recognizes
      revenue when it satisfies a performance obligation by transferring control over a product or service to a restaurant guest, retail customer or other customer.&#160; The Company recognizes revenues from restaurant sales when payment is tendered at the
      point of sale, as the Company&#8217;s performance obligation to provide food and beverages is satisfied.&#160; The Company recognizes revenues from retail sales when payment is tendered at the point of sale, as the Company&#8217;s performance obligation to provide
      merchandise is satisfied.&#160; Ecommerce sales, including shipping revenue, are recorded upon delivery to the customer.&#160; Additionally, the Company provides for estimated returns based on return history and sales levels.&#160; The Company&#8217;s policy is to
      present sales in the Consolidated Statements of Income on a net presentation basis after deducting sales tax.</div>

</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606065" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606066"><ix:continuation id="Text_088353689342412f9ad6aa54a43776e32">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Included in restaurant and retail revenue is gift card breakage.&#160; Customer purchases of gift cards, to be utilized at
      the Company&#8217;s stores, are not recognized as sales until the card is redeemed and the customer purchases food and/or merchandise.&#160; Gift cards do not carry an expiration date; therefore, customers can redeem their gift cards indefinitely. A certain
      number of gift cards will not be fully redeemed. Management estimates unredeemed balances and recognizes gift card breakage revenue for these amounts in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Income over the expected redemption period.&#160; Gift card
      breakage is recognized when the likelihood of a gift card being redeemed by the customer is remote and the Company determines that there is not a legal obligation to remit the unredeemed gift card balance to the relevant jurisdiction.&#160; The
      determination of the gift card breakage rate is based upon the Company&#8217;s specific historical redemption patterns. The Company recognizes gift card breakage by applying its estimate of the rate of gift card breakage over the period of estimated
      redemption.&#160; For 2023, 2022 and 2021, gift card breakage was $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:GiftCardBreakageRevenue" id="Fact_a5f877e38ff74533b3ea20a12cd154dd" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">10,713</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:GiftCardBreakageRevenue" id="Fact_8982e6181b944e14a26fc35685432f11" contextRef="c20210731to20220729" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">9,572</ix:nonFraction>, and $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:GiftCardBreakageRevenue" id="Fact_937a2f39f5b24572bc702e365b32af2a" contextRef="c20200801to20210730" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">6,349</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.&#160; Revenue recognized in the Consolidated
      Statements of Income for 2023, 2022 and 2021, respectively, for the redemption of gift cards which were included in the deferred revenue balance at the beginning of the fiscal year was $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRevenueRecognizedForRedemptionOfGiftCards" id="Fact_07a8443638e6413a8293534e50fa2eb5" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">40,103</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRevenueRecognizedForRedemptionOfGiftCards" id="Fact_7182270a959a4d0faae95f74d047a2b7" contextRef="c20210731to20220729" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">42,169</ix:nonFraction>, and $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRevenueRecognizedForRedemptionOfGiftCards" id="Fact_1e0472106ed249d6829305c2fd2a296d" contextRef="c20200801to20210730" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">42,266</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.&#160; Deferred revenue related to the Company&#8217;s gift cards was $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRelatedToGiftCards" id="Fact_39787bb4fe674f548b9b3c11d03a886b" contextRef="c20230728" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">88,566</ix:nonFraction>
      and $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRelatedToGiftCards" id="Fact_b82e07a9e65f49a7b35fba4b3a2c2428" contextRef="c20220729" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">93,569</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, at July 28, 2023 and July 29, 2022.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606066" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606067">
<div style="text-align: left; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:InsuranceDisclosureTextBlock" id="Text_31b33bcc69cb4c619d1a4ae5a84df9c4" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_95c3d57c549b4e218e093393e9b57efe1"><ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606067" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606068">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Insurance &#8211; The Company self-insures a significant portion of its workers&#8217; compensation and general liability programs.&#160;
      The Company purchases insurance for individual workers&#8217; compensation claims that exceed $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ThresholdAmountForWorkersCompensationInsuranceLevel1" id="Fact_67665761552f4a519edd865326c300be" contextRef="c20200801to20210730" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal"><ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ThresholdAmountForWorkersCompensationInsuranceLevel1" id="Fact_37ba99b4f4d74937aef0e01136e1f7f9" contextRef="c20210731to20220729" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal"><ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ThresholdAmountForWorkersCompensationInsuranceLevel1" id="Fact_20f96430159b4e6688e53662cb5d83b9" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">750</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> or $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ThresholdAmountForWorkersCompensationInsuranceLevel2" id="Fact_0d20992db5114292a60cda4983fd870c" contextRef="c20200801to20210730" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal"><ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ThresholdAmountForWorkersCompensationInsuranceLevel2" id="Fact_a8d40887ec4a4656a64884d19ed9c7f6" contextRef="c20210731to20220729" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal"><ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ThresholdAmountForWorkersCompensationInsuranceLevel2" id="Fact_b83d52c850d04cd5aecae305e2ce7b31" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1,000</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> depending on the state in which the claim originates.&#160; The Company purchases insurance for individual general liability claims that exceed $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ThresholdAmountForGeneralLiabilityInsurance" id="Fact_33defbd9aab14123a424f61d6336c4c1" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">500</ix:nonFraction>.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_95c3d57c549b4e218e093393e9b57efe1" continuedAt="Text_95c3d57c549b4e218e093393e9b57efe2"><ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606068" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606069">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: left; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><br />
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_95c3d57c549b4e218e093393e9b57efe2" continuedAt="Text_95c3d57c549b4e218e093393e9b57efe3"><ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606069" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606070">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company records a reserve for workers&#8217; compensation and general liability for all unresolved claims and for an
      estimate of incurred but not reported claims (&#8220;IBNR&#8221;).&#160; These reserves and estimates of IBNR claims are based upon a full scope actuarial study which is performed annually at the end of the Company&#8217;s third quarter and is adjusted by the actuarially
      determined losses and actual claims payments for the fourth quarter.&#160; Additionally, the Company performs limited scope actuarial studies on a quarterly basis to verify and/or modify the Company&#8217;s reserves. The reserves and losses in the actuarial
      study represent a range of possible outcomes within which no given estimate is more likely than any other estimate.&#160; As such, the Company records the losses at the lower half of that range and discounts them to present value using a risk-free
      interest rate based on projected timing of payments. The Company also monitors actual claims development, including incurrence or settlement of individual large claims during the interim periods between actuarial studies as another means of
      estimating the adequacy of its reserves.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <div><ix:continuation id="Text_95c3d57c549b4e218e093393e9b57efe3" continuedAt="Text_95c3d57c549b4e218e093393e9b57efe4"><ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606070" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606071">

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s group health plans combine the use of self-insured and fully-insured programs.&#160; Benefits for any
      individual (employee or dependents) in the self-insured program are limited.&#160; The Company records a liability for the self-insured portion of its group health program for all unpaid claims based upon a loss development analysis derived from actual
      group health claims payment experience.&#160; The Company also records a liability for unpaid prescription drug claims based on historical experience.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Store pre-opening costs &#8211; Start-up costs of a new store are expensed when incurred.</div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606075" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606076"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_fa216b6707f3481799db70b814d2e5ca" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_d84065ce689c409e83750f772af3ab371">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; color: #000000;">Leases &#8211; </span>The Company&#8217;s leases are
      classified as either finance or operating leases.&#160; The Company has ground leases for its leased stores and office space leases that are recorded as operating leases under various non-cancellable operating leases.&#160; The Company also leases its
      advertising billboards, vehicle fleets and certain equipment under various non-cancellable operating leases.&#160; To determine whether a contract is or contains a lease, the Company determines at contract inception whether it contains the right to
      control the use of an identified asset for a period of time in exchange for consideration.&#160; If the contract has the right to obtain substantially all of the economic benefit from use of the identified asset and the right to direct the use of the
      identified asset, the Company recognizes a right-of-use asset and lease liability.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606076" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606077"><ix:continuation id="Text_d84065ce689c409e83750f772af3ab371" continuedAt="Text_d84065ce689c409e83750f772af3ab372">

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <br />
    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606077" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606078"><ix:continuation id="Text_d84065ce689c409e83750f772af3ab372">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s leases all have varying terms and expire at various dates through 2058. Restaurant leases typically have base terms of <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="Fact_c1e35241211943508e6638b3c4ab5db1" contextRef="c20230728_MajorPropertyClassAxis_RestaurantStoresMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">ten years</ix:nonNumeric> with <ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:NumberOfOptionalRenewalPeriods" id="Fact_1a6ccd73cccc4f3c9024249edaa2189a" contextRef="c20220730to20230728_MajorPropertyClassAxis_RestaurantStoresMember_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" unitRef="U007" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">four</ix:nonFraction> to <ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:NumberOfOptionalRenewalPeriods" id="Fact_51fe74f0b6444d89a1519fcc9212c92b" contextRef="c20220730to20230728_MajorPropertyClassAxis_RestaurantStoresMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" unitRef="U007" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">five</ix:nonFraction> optional renewal periods of <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" id="Fact_2acb1c6f10ed44be8f8f086573f539cd" contextRef="c20230728_MajorPropertyClassAxis_RestaurantStoresMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric>
      each.&#160; The Company uses a lease life that generally begins on the commencement date, including the rent holiday periods, and generally extends through certain renewal periods that can be exercised at the Company&#8217;s option.&#160; During rent holiday
      periods, which include the pre-opening period during construction, the Company has possession of and access to the property, but is not obligated to, and normally does not, make rent payments.&#160;&#160; The Company has included lease renewal options in the
      lease term for calculations of the right-of-use asset and liability for which at the commencement of the lease it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise those renewal options.&#160; Additionally, some of the leases have contingent rent
      provisions and others require adjustments for inflation or index.&#160;&#160; Contingent rent is determined as a percentage of gross sales in excess of specified levels. The Company records a contingent rent liability and corresponding rent expense when it is
      probable sales have been achieved in amounts in excess of the specified levels.&#160; The Company&#8217;s lease agreements do not contain any material residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; color: #000000;">.</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606085" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606086"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="Text_89f623a65d494ed38fa0acc1b6c54e9e" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc11">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Share-based compensation &#8211; The Company&#8217;s share-based compensation consists of nonvested stock awards and units.&#160;
      Share-based compensation is recorded in general and administrative expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Income.&#160; Share-based compensation expense is recognized based on the grant date fair value and the achievement of performance conditions for
      certain awards.&#160; The Company recognizes share-based compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period, which is generally the award&#8217;s vesting period, or to the date on which retirement eligibility is achieved, if
      shorter.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606086" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606087"><ix:continuation id="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc11" continuedAt="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc12">
<div><br />
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606087" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606088"><ix:continuation id="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc12" continuedAt="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc13">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Certain nonvested stock awards and units contain performance conditions.&#160; Compensation expense for performance-based
      awards is recognized when it is probable that the performance criteria will be met.&#160; If any performance goals are not met, no compensation expense is ultimately recognized and, to the extent previously recognized, compensation expense is reversed.&#160;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606088" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606089"><ix:continuation id="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc13" continuedAt="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc14">
<div><br />
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606089" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606090"><ix:continuation id="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc14" continuedAt="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc15">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">If a share-based compensation award is modified after the grant date, incremental compensation expense is recognized in
      an amount equal to the excess of the fair value of the modified award over the fair value of the original award immediately before the modification.&#160; Incremental compensation expense for vested awards is recognized immediately.&#160; For unvested awards,
      the sum of the incremental compensation expense and the remaining unrecognized compensation expense for the original award on the modification date is recognized over the modified service period.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606090" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606091"><ix:continuation id="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc15" continuedAt="Text_8f4be838608b422fb0c9294998ad2bc16">

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Additionally, the Company&#8217;s policy is to issue shares of common stock to satisfy exercises of share-based compensation
      awards.</div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606093" continuedAt="Text_d84bd1c3fd7342b3b1d64969c368606094"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_4931c19fe2c14932ba5d3a64d7039419" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" escape="true">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Income taxes &#8211; The Company&#8217;s provision for income taxes includes employer tax credits for FICA taxes paid on employee
      tip income and other employer tax credits are accounted for by the flow-through method.&#160; Deferred income taxes reflect the net tax effects of temporary differences between the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities for financial reporting
      purposes and the amounts used for income tax purposes.&#160; The Company recognizes (or derecognizes) a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return in the financial statements when it is more likely than not (i.e., a likelihood of more than
      fifty percent) that the position would be sustained (or not sustained) upon examination by tax authorities.&#160; A recognized tax position is then measured at the largest amount of benefit that is greater than fifty percent likely of being realized upon
      ultimate settlement.&#160; The Company recognizes, net of tax, interest and estimated penalties related to uncertain tax positions in its provision for income taxes.&#160; See Note 12 for additional information regarding income taxes.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">N</span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 24px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">et income per share &#8211; Basic consolidated net income
        per share is computed by dividing consolidated net income available to common shareholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for the reporting period.&#160; Diluted consolidated net income per share reflects the potential
        dilution that could occur if securities, options or other contracts to issue common stock were exercised or converted into common stock and is based upon the weighted average number of common and common equivalent shares outstanding during the
        reporting period. Common equivalent shares related to nonvested stock awards and units issued by the Company are calculated using the treasury stock method.&#160; The outstanding nonvested stock awards and units issued by the Company represent the only
        dilutive effects on diluted consolidated net income per share. Prior to the adoption of new accounting guidance for convertible instruments in 2022, the Company&#8217;s convertible senior notes and related warrants were calculated using the treasury
        stock method.&#160; Beginning in 2022, the convertible senior notes and related warrants are calculated using the net share settlement option under the if-converted method.&#160; Because the principal amount of the convertible senior notes will be settled in
        cash with any excess conversion value settled in cash or shares of common stock, the convertible senior notes have been excluded from the computation of diluted earnings per share because the average market price of the Company&#8217;s common stock

      <ix:continuation id="Text_3bb6448373d24fefaf49297ba5cce36427"><ix:continuation id="Text_c06f75d90f9049f498ffd1c886c65b9a14">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">During 2023, <ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:NumberOfLocationsDeterminedToBeImpaired" id="Fact_6925c05ccd784d9ea5e4c293902a1a24" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U005" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">six</ix:nonFraction>
        Cracker Barrel locations were determined to be impaired because of declining operating performance.&#160; Fair value of these locations was determined by sales prices of comparable assets or estimates of discounted future cash flows considering their
        highest and best use.&#160; Assumptions used in the cash flow model included projected annual revenue growth rates and projected cash flows, which can be affected by economic conditions and management&#8217;s expectations.&#160; Additionally, changes in the local
        and national economies and markets for real estate and other assets can impact the sales prices of the assets.&#160; The Company has determined that the majority of the inputs used to value its long-lived assets held and used are unobservable inputs,
        and thus, are considered Level 3 inputs.&#160; Based on its analysis, the Company recorded an impairment charge of $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseImpairmentLoss" id="Fact_da0fe38925854431b060a2ecf30780a8" contextRef="c20220730to20230728" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">11,692</ix:nonFraction>, which is included
        in the impairment and store closing costs line on the Consolidated Statement of Income.</div>

<div style="text-align: left; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Convertible Note Hedge and Warrant Transactions</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_15230c80569847028f6d7fed73b3ff1758" continuedAt="Text_15230c80569847028f6d7fed73b3ff1759">

      <ix:continuation id="Text_15230c80569847028f6d7fed73b3ff1760" continuedAt="Text_15230c80569847028f6d7fed73b3ff1761">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;">In connection with the offering of the
          Notes, the Company entered into convertible note hedge transactions (the &#8220;Convertible Note Hedge Transactions&#8221;) with certain of the initial purchasers of the Notes and/or their respective affiliates and other financial institutions (in this
          capacity, the &#8220;Hedge Counterparties&#8221;). Concurrently with the Company&#8217;s entry into the Convertible Note Hedge Transactions, the Company also entered into separate, warrant transactions with the Hedge Counterparties collectively relating to the
          same number of shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, which initially is approximately </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif;"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" id="Fact_627028c1ee9945e6b824771e8018d910" contextRef="c20230728_DebtInstrumentAxis_Zero625PercentConvertibleSeniorNotesDue2026Member" unitRef="U002" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1,600,000</ix:nonFraction><span style="font-size: 10pt;"> shares, subject to customary anti-dilution adjustments, and for which the Company received proceeds that partially offset the cost of entering into the Convertible Note Hedge Transactions (the &#8220;Warrant Transactions&#8221;).</span></span></div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The Convertible Note Hedge
        Transactions cover, subject to customary anti-dilution adjustments, the number of shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock that initially underlie the Notes, and are expected generally to reduce the potential equity dilution, and/or offset any cash
        payments in excess of the principal amount due, as the case may be, upon conversion of the Notes.</span> By default, the Warrant Transactions are net share settled and the Company has the option to settle in cash or shares.<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> The Warrant Transactions could have a dilutive effect on the Company&#8217;s common stock to the extent that the price of its common stock exceeds the strike price of the Warrant
        Transactions. The strike price was initially $</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman',Times,serif;"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" id="Fact_d34285d55487432dad02589e7a9e1c7d" contextRef="c20230728_DebtInstrumentAxis_Zero625PercentConvertibleSeniorNotesDue2026Member" unitRef="U003" decimals="2" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">263.39</ix:nonFraction><span style="font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> per share and is subject to certain adjustments under the terms of the Warrant Transactions. </span>On July 28, 2023, the strike price, as adjusted, of the Warrant Transactions was adjusted to $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:ClassOfWarrantOrRightsAdjustedExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights" id="Fact_d3a81020c6ff43a1bbcde3d50bd38a6a" contextRef="c20230728_DebtInstrumentAxis_Zero625PercentConvertibleSeniorNotesDue2026Member" unitRef="U003" decimals="2" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">237.73</ix:nonFraction> per share as a result of dividends declared since the Notes were issued.</span> </div>
</ix:continuation>

          paid-in capital on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheet during 2021.</span></span> </div>

<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">5. Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_dca76ac7888d4f6ca026fbc76c51d6fe1" continuedAt="Text_dca76ac7888d4f6ca026fbc76c51d6fe2">
<div><br />
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_dca76ac7888d4f6ca026fbc76c51d6fe2" continuedAt="Text_dca76ac7888d4f6ca026fbc76c51d6fe3">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">During the fourth quarter of 2021, in conjunction with paying down debt under the revolving credit facility, the Company
      terminated all of its interest rate swap agreements which resulted in the reclassification of the remaining losses from accumulated other comprehensive loss (&#8220;AOCL&#8221;) to the Consolidated Statements of Income as part of interest expense.&#160;&#160; The
      determination of the amounts reclassified from AOCL to interest expense was based on the Company&#8217;s assessment that the forecasted transactions under the hedging relationships were no longer probable.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_dca76ac7888d4f6ca026fbc76c51d6fe3" continuedAt="Text_dca76ac7888d4f6ca026fbc76c51d6fe4">

    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_dca76ac7888d4f6ca026fbc76c51d6fe4" continuedAt="Text_dca76ac7888d4f6ca026fbc76c51d6fe5">

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;">Prior to the termination of the interest
        rate swaps, for each of the Company&#8217;s interest rate swaps, the Company had agreed to exchange with a counterparty the difference between fixed and variable interest amounts calculated by reference to an agreed-upon notional principal amount.&#160; The
        interest rates on the portion of the Company&#8217;s outstanding debt covered by its interest rate swaps were fixed at the rates specified in the interest rate swap agreements plus the Company&#8217;s credit spread. </span>All of the Company&#8217;s interest rate
      swaps were accounted for as cash flow hedges.</div>
</ix:continuation>

        stock at management&#8217;s discretion up to a total value of $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" id="Fact_328beb8e41f9469a8182184a58d1fb0c" contextRef="c20220729" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">200,000</ix:nonFraction>; this authorization replaced the previous unused portion of the previous

<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">8. Leases</div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_e6a106cc9a8e40ea983123bab69245bd1" continuedAt="Text_e6a106cc9a8e40ea983123bab69245bd2">

    <ix:continuation id="Text_e6a106cc9a8e40ea983123bab69245bd2" continuedAt="Text_e6a106cc9a8e40ea983123bab69245bd3">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; color: #000000;">In 2020</span>,<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; color: #000000;"> the Company adopted new accounting guidance for leases.&#160; As part of the adoption of this accounting guidance for leases, the Company elected to not separate lease and non-lease
        components.&#160;&#160; Additionally, the Company elected to apply the short term lease exemption to all asset classes and the short term lease expense for the period reasonably reflects the short term lease commitments.&#160; As the Company&#8217;s leases do not
        provide an implicit rate, the Company uses the incremental borrowing rate based on the information available at the time of commencement or modification date in determining the present value of lease payments. For operating leases that commenced
        prior to the date of adoption of the new lease accounting guidance, the Company used the incremental borrowing rate as of the adoption date.&#160; Assumptions used in determining the Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate include the Company&#8217;s implied
        credit rating and an estimate of secured borrowing rates based on comparable market data.</span></div>
</ix:continuation>

      has not yet taken possession. <div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In 2009, the Company completed sale and leaseback transactions involving <ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:NumberOfStoresInvolvingSaleLeasebackTransaction" id="Fact_4f2887c7e34146b2a7ba49c7318166bb" contextRef="c20080802to20090731_MajorPropertyClassAxis_OwnedStoresMember_SaleLeasebackTransactionDescriptionAxis_SaleLeasebackTransactionsIn2009Member" unitRef="U010" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">15</ix:nonFraction> of its owned stores and its retail distribution center.&#160; Under the transactions, the land, buildings and improvements at the locations were sold and leased back for terms of <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="Fact_19b8b9bd70f24c74ba22e85c0da4d55e" contextRef="c20230728_MajorPropertyClassAxis_OwnedStoresMember_SaleLeasebackTransactionDescriptionAxis_SaleLeasebackTransactionsIn2009Member" format="ixt-sec:duryear">20</ix:nonNumeric> and <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="Fact_b978bffdda1b4af085d1a0b2d2d5ce0f" contextRef="c20230728_MajorPropertyClassAxis_RetailDistributionCenterMember_SaleLeasebackTransactionDescriptionAxis_SaleLeasebackTransactionsIn2009Member" format="ixt-sec:duryear">15</ix:nonNumeric> years, respectively.&#160; Equipment

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In 2000, the Company completed a sale and leaseback transaction involving <ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:NumberOfStoresInvolvingSaleLeasebackTransaction" id="Fact_0389cc08f99e4d62b3811536cf863b1d" contextRef="c20200729to20200729_MajorPropertyClassAxis_OwnedStoresMember_SaleLeasebackTransactionDescriptionAxis_SaleLeasebackTransactionsIn2000Member" unitRef="U010" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">65</ix:nonFraction> of its owned Cracker Barrel stores.&#160; Under the transaction, the land, buildings and building improvements at the locations were sold and leased back for a term of <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="Fact_d484343c94354b38b92acc5e8479c6f9" contextRef="c20230728_MajorPropertyClassAxis_OwnedStoresMember_SaleLeasebackTransactionDescriptionAxis_SaleLeasebackTransactionsIn2000Member" format="ixt-sec:duryear">21</ix:nonNumeric> years.&#160; The leases for these stores included specified renewal options for up to <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" id="Fact_9e07571656704d19839968e4b2bc5410" contextRef="c20230728_MajorPropertyClassAxis_OwnedStoresMember_SaleLeasebackTransactionDescriptionAxis_SaleLeasebackTransactionsIn2000Member" format="ixt-sec:duryear">20</ix:nonNumeric> additional years.&#160; On July 29, 2020, the Company entered into an agreement with the original lessor and a third-party financier to obtain ownership of&#160;<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:NumberOfStoresCompletedInSaleLeasebackTransaction" id="Fact_7e1b272cd1234c0d980102d6d44c8f09" contextRef="c20200729to20200729_MajorPropertyClassAxis_OwnedStoresMember_SaleLeasebackTransactionDescriptionAxis_SaleLeasebackTransactionsIn2000Member" unitRef="U010" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">64</ix:nonFraction>&#160;of the <ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:NumberOfStoresInvolvingSaleLeasebackTransaction" id="Fact_daa5c430463a4258924c227d24c234da" contextRef="c20200729to20200729_MajorPropertyClassAxis_OwnedStoresMember_SaleLeasebackTransactionDescriptionAxis_SaleLeasebackTransactionsIn2000Member" unitRef="U010" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">65</ix:nonFraction> Cracker Barrel properties and
      simultaneously entered into a sale and leaseback transaction with the financier for an aggregate purchase price, net of closing costs, of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:SaleLeasebackTransactionNetBookValue" id="Fact_36c0c2a9dad54f0db67312f8ecc3c952" contextRef="c20200729_MajorPropertyClassAxis_OwnedStoresMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">198,083</ix:nonFraction>.
      The Company purchased the remaining property for approximately $<ix:nonFraction name="cbrl:RemainingPropertyPurchased" id="Fact_25de36f212b6460d9b32e75d4bf12b29" contextRef="c20230728_SaleLeasebackTransactionDescriptionAxis_SaleLeasebackTransactionsIn2000Member" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">3,200</ix:nonFraction>. In connection with the sale and leaseback transaction, the Company

<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">9. Share-Based Compensation</div>
</ix:nonNumeric>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a002" continuedAt="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a003">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Stock Compensation Plans</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a003" continuedAt="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a004">
<div style="text-align: left; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a004" continuedAt="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a005">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s employee compensation plans are administered by the Compensation Committee of the Company&#8217;s Board of
      Directors (the &#8220;Committee&#8221;).&#160; The Committee is authorized to determine, at time periods within its discretion and subject to the direction of the Board of Directors, which employees will be granted awards, the number of shares covered by any awards
      granted, and within applicable limits, the terms and provisions relating to the exercise and vesting of any awards.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a005" continuedAt="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a006">
<div><br />
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a006" continuedAt="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a007">
<div style="display:none;"><br /></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt; color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">On November 19, 2020, the Company&#8217;s shareholders approved the 2020 Omnibus Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2020 Omnibus Plan&#8221;)
      which became effective on that date. The 2020 Omnibus Plan authorizes the following types of awards for employees and non-employee directors: stock options, stock appreciation rights, nonvested stock, restricted stock units, other share-based awards
      and performance awards. After the effective date of the 2020 Omnibus Plan, <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesShareBasedCompensation" id="Fact_dbadad279ff4483c966490cad68a40f1" contextRef="c20220730to20230728_PlanNameAxis_OmnibusPlan2010Member" unitRef="U002" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> additional awards could be granted under the Company&#8217;s 2010
      Omnibus Incentive Stock and Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Prior Plan&#8221;).</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a007" continuedAt="Text_e6a9f091c0dc41c1ad05fd726b729a008">
<div><br />
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
